messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alice Johnson <alice.j@fintechco.com>, Bob Lee <bob.lee@fintechco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 8 Mar 2027 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity pricing qualification - FinTechCo (GPU, throughput, budget)

Hi Alice / Bob — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and next steps so we all have the same plan.

Recap (from today’s discovery):
- Estimated average monthly tokens: ~1.2B tokens/month (1,200,000,000).
- Peak / burst: up to ~2.0B tokens in high-month scenarios; traffic has strong diurnal spikes.
- Average prompt size: 600–1,200 tokens per request (mix of short prompts and long-context LLM calls).
- Concurrency expectation: ~50–120 concurrent active requests during peak hours.

Technical sizing / customer asks:
- Preferred GPU types: H100 80GB (preferred for latency and larger context/quantized workloads) or A100 80GB (fallback if H100 capacity constrained).
- Target reserved capacity: exploring 8–16 GPUs to start (we discussed 12 as a likely sweet spot based on current volumes).
- Throughput targets: sustain ~50k tokens/sec (sustained) with burst capacity to ~150k tokens/sec; translate this to ~60–100 QPS depending on avg tokens per call.

Budget / unit economics discussion:
- Customer target $/1M tokens: aiming for ~$1,000–$1,200 per 1M tokens as their target unit expense.
- Monthly budget range discussed: roughly $45k–$75k/month for a reserved solution, depending on GPU type and commitment term.

Next steps (action owners):
1) Rishi — share a pricing worksheet that maps 8/12/16 GPU reserved configurations to estimated $/1M tokens (will include both H100 and A100 math). (Attachment: redwood_dedicated_pricing_v1.pdf) — by EOD Tuesday.
2) Alice/Bob — send detailed hourly traffic profile (CSV) and any region constraints (we heard you prefer us-east-1).
3) Marissa / Marcus — review recommended rollout (canary + autoscale policies + fallback model variant) and confirm latency SLO tradeoffs.

If that looks right, suggest a 30-min follow-up on Thurs to review the worksheet and pick a model for the SOW.

Thanks —
Rishi

Thanks Rishi — helpful summary. A couple clarifications from our side:
- Monthly token numbers: the 1.2B is our current projection for the first 6 months, but we want pricing that tolerates +50% growth without a major re-architecture.
- Budget: $45k–$75k is the right range for a committed, reserved price. If H100 is required, we may skew to the higher end.
- Region: yes, must be hosted in us-east-1 (compliance + latency for customers).

Could you please include in the worksheet a simple sensitivity table: 8 / 12 / 16 GPUs × H100 vs A100 and the implied $/1M tokens at our projected (1.2B) and at +50%? Also confirm expected latency SLOs per config (p50/p95 generation latency for a 1k-token request).

I’ll get the hourly traffic export to you by EOD today.

— Alice

alice.j@fintechco.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 9 Mar 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: preliminary pricing math for FinTechCo (private note)

Internal calc (quick):
- Baseline assumptions: 12 × H100 (reserved, sustained) with smart batching, prefix KV caching, and 95% utilization during business hours.
- Cost model (rough): infra & amortized HW + SW + ops = $Xk/month per GPU (we keep the real numbers internal). Using current unit math this maps to an estimated customer-facing rate of ~$900 per 1M tokens at 1.2B tokens/month on 12 H100s.
- For A100 80GB equivalent config (12 × A100) the unit economics are ~10–20% worse, putting customer-facing $/1M tokens closer to $1,050–$1,100 depending on batching efficiency.
- 8 GPUs: results in higher $/1M tokens (~1.3x) due to lower parallelism and batching headroom; 16 GPUs : slightly lower $/1M (~0.9x) but higher absolute monthly commitment.

Latency SLOs (rough p50/p95 for 1k-token gen):
- 12 × H100, tuned runtime: p50 ~250–400ms, p95 ~1.2–1.8s (depends on model selection & quantization).
- 12 × A100: p50 ~300–500ms, p95 ~1.5–2.2s.

Recommendation: present 3 options to the customer (8/12/16) for both H100 and A100 with explicit $/1M tokens and monthly commit. Rishi — I can draft the numbers into the attached worksheet and flag where we may need legal for GPU addendum if they insist on H100-only.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity pricing qualification - FinTechCo (GPU, throughput, budget)

Alice — thanks for the clarifications and for committing to the traffic export. Per Marissa’s notes above, I’ve attached a clean pricing worksheet that lays out the 8 / 12 / 16 GPU options for H100 and A100, and a sensitivity view at 1.2B and 1.8B tokens/month. Highlights:

- Example line items (from attachment):
  • 12 × H100 (12-mo committed): est $900 / 1M tokens at 1.2B tokens/mo; est $820 / 1M tokens at 1.8B tokens/mo (volume discount and higher utilization).
  • 12 × A100 (12-mo committed): est $1,050 / 1M tokens at 1.2B tokens/mo.
  • 8 × H100 (short term): higher per-token rate (~$1,170 / 1M) but lower monthly commitment.

- Region: we confirm availability in us-east-1 and will scope the private VPC/networking in the SOW.
- Latency: included p50/p95 estimates per config (see sheet).

Attached: redwood_dedicated_pricing_v1.pdf (pricing worksheet) and a draft SOW (mvp-sow-draft.docx).

Next steps:
1) Alice/Bob — confirm whether you prefer H100-only or if A100 is acceptable (this materially affects pricing).
2) Customer to send the hourly traffic profile (CSV).
3) If agreeable, we’ll book a 30-min review on Thurs to finalize selected configuration and sign the SOW.

Happy to hop on a call — give me a couple of 30-min windows that work for you.

Best,
Rishi
